title: OpenReading Journal Record v0.1
description: One line of a run's JSONL journal (internal/design/ledger.md §6, §11). T1's JsonlJournal writes exactly one JournalRecord per Journal.append call, and a leaf's full history under one step_id is [attempted, <terminal>] in append order (§8, resolving Phase A round-2 F1 — Journal.get(key) returns every record at a key, never a single value). Self-contained (does not $ref step.v0.1.json) per this repo's existing per-family schema convention — the shape mirrors StepResult deliberately, since T1 journals a StepResult verbatim with no separate envelope.

started_epoch_ms.description: Absolute UTC epoch milliseconds (wall clock, Clock.now_wall_ms) at which the dispatch was issued. Not a monotonic reading: this value is written by one process and read by another, so it must name a moment, not measure an interval.

ended_epoch_ms.description: Absolute UTC epoch milliseconds (wall clock, Clock.now_wall_ms) at which the step reached a terminal outcome. Subtracting started_epoch_ms gives elapsed wall time, which a clock adjustment can distort; the engine measures its own durations off the monotonic clock instead.

journal_seq.description: Ledger T3 (§4.1/§7.4): a per-run monotonic append count, assigned by Journal.append — the record's own replay-stable completion order.
